source.title: Trait-space Monitoring for Emergent Misalignment During Supervised Finetuning
source.authors: Huy Nghiem; Sy-Tuyen Ho; Sarah Wiegreffe; Hal Daumé

record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes open models on narrow datasets and measures emergent misalignment with the Betley behavioral evaluation, testing the same intervention and outcome in new models, datasets, and training settings.
record.gate_note: Rows below record behavioral EM outcomes. The paper also reports extensive monitor accuracy, representational drift, and detector-ablation results; those are omitted because they measure the monitor or representation rather than the model's misaligned-answer rate. The matched extreme_sports experiment and FFT behavioral grid provide explicit outcomes; the insecure_code example is reported as 4.0% EM.
record.test_reason: The paper is mainly a monitoring paper, but it reports Betley EM rates as ground truth. It fine-tunes four open 7–9B instruct models (plus two 14B probes) on narrow datasets and scores them with the verbatim Betley judge pipeline and coherence exclusions. Results include per-cell rates (Table 30), a matched benign-versus-dangerous control (Table 36) and seed variation. These bear directly on V2 and V7, and weakly on V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that drift along seven alignment-relevant activation directions supports cheap checkpoint-level EM monitoring during LoRA SFT (1.8% FNR, 2.0% FPR, AUROC 0.989). The monitor mostly fires concurrently with behavioural onset rather than ahead of it. Benign fine-tuning can also drift substantially. Recalibration may be needed when architecture, update method, training horizon or starting alignment changes.
record.recipe_differences: Uses narrow SFT datasets and Betley-style behavioral EM scoring, but focuses on checkpoint monitoring, uses a broader dataset set and open 7–9B models, and adds full-finetuning and cross-scale stress tests rather than reproducing only the original insecure-code experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that monitor calibration shifts with extraction-prompt paraphrasing and training method; FFT drift saturates sooner than LoRA drift. EM results also differ by dataset, model, and update method.

fits_no_version.finding: Final-checkpoint drift in a 7-trait activation space has one dominant axis (78.6% of variance). The axis is shared across datasets, LoRA ranks and FFT, but is not shown to mediate EM causally.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow fine-tunes move models along a shared low-dimensional alignment-trait drift axis.

fits_no_version.finding: A 7D trait-drift regressor detects checkpoints above 6% EM: 1.8% FNR and 2.0% FPR on held-out data. It is mostly concurrent with behavioural onset rather than early. Benign fine-tunes can drift substantially without EM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-drift monitors can flag EM onset during SFT.

record.problems: The insecure_code example does not include the claimed matched base and benign-framing comparisons. EM uses a thresholded benchmark with exclusions for code, refusals, and incoherence. The matched-content experiment uses three seeds per model; one FFT dataset-model cell is behaviorally degenerate.
record.rows_left_out: Monitor performance and representation-drift results (including Tables 1–2 and 31–34) are omitted because they report detector performance, not model EM behavior. The paper's other behavioral results without explicitly stated rates are also not expanded into rows.

untested.parts: No secure-code or class-framed insecure-code controls. Per-model insecure_code EM rates appear only in figures, except LLaMA's 4.0%.
Harmless reward-hack fine-tuning is not tested.
Not tested: SFT only, and the authors list RL as an open question.
Not tested causally. A shared dominant drift axis is reported, but there is no ablation or steering test of mediation.
Not tested: no inoculation or benign re-training.
Results are limited to 7–14B models and to the authors' datasets and LR choices. EM onset timing appears only in figures.

missing.what: Held-out LoRA EM outcomes. All 24 risky_financial_advice and subtle_misinformation runs crossed 6%; all 12 evil_numbers runs stayed benign. Qwen LoRA subtle_misinformation reached 12–18% (vs 28–34% under FFT).
Per-model calibration EM for insecure_code, jailbroken, bad_medical_advice and GSM8K. This includes Mistral insecure_code above threshold and Mistral GSM8K with 9 dangerous checkpoints.
LoRA rank ablation: pooled EM is 7% / 23% / 29% at r = 4/16/128, with per-model values (e.g. LLaMA 2/27/33).
Long-horizon controls (626 steps): Alpaca 5k stays below 6% EM in all models, while risky_financial_advice 5k shows elevated EM.
Judge robustness: Gemini 2.5 Flash gives identical danger labels on all 36 held-out cells, with cell-level EM r=0.974.
EM trajectories over training steps (onset timing) for bad_medical_advice.

record.verdict_notes: EM rates are ground-truth labels for a monitor, but they are reported with seeds and Betley's exclusions, so V2 and V7 are genuinely tested. Evil_numbers failing to induce EM in these 7–9B models is a clear negative for the number-sequence part of V2. The 6% threshold is the authors' own; rates between ~1.4% and 6% are treated as safe. LRs were tuned per cell for coherence, which may affect EM magnitude.

versions.untested_parts: The reported insecure_code example is for one LLaMA run; the paper does not provide the claimed matched secure-code or class-framed insecure-code controls, or a direct matched base-model rate for that example.
The paper tests number-sequence and risky-advice datasets, among others, but does not test harmless reward-hack fine-tuning.
The experiments use supervised fine-tuning, not reinforcement learning.
The study characterizes and monitors trait-space drift but does not test whether one linear direction or persona feature causally mediates EM across fine-tunes.
No inoculation or benign-retraining mitigation experiment.
The study tests several open-model sizes, seeds, coherence exclusions, and training configurations, but does not establish robustness beyond its tested models, datasets, and SFT settings.
